article_title: An Increase in Emotional Support, a Reduction in Negative Social Emotional Skills, or Both?: Examining How Universal Social Emotional Programs Achieve Reductions in Aggression
citation: Portnow, S., Downer, J., & Brown, J. (2015). An Increase in Emotional Support, A Reduction in Negative Social Emotional Skills, Or Both?: Examining How Universal Social Emotional Programs Achieve Reductions in Aggression. SREE Spring 2015 Conference. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED555659
title: 4Rs+MTP: Integrated SEL and literacy program with video-based coaching
description: The 4Rs program has "two primary components: (1) a comprehensive 7-unit, 21 lesson, literacy-based curriculum in conflict resolution and social-emotional learning and (2) 25 hours of teacher training, plus ongoing coaching." MyTeachingPartner (MTP) supplements this with "8 MTP coaching cycles throughout the academic year" in which teachers videotape instruction, receive edited video segments and written prompts on a private website, and meet with a coach for a 30-minute conference.
requirements: Teachers videotape their implementation of instructional activities every two weeks
constraints: Implemented in 6 New York City public elementary schools with 35 teachers from grades 3-5
examples: Each unit begins with the teacher reading aloud a children's book, followed by "Book Talk" discussion, writing, and role-playing
key_sources: Portnow, S., Downer, J., & Brown, J. (2015). An Increase in Emotional Support, A Reduction in Negative Social Emotional Skills, Or Both?: Examining How Universal Social Emotional Programs Achieve Reductions in Aggression. SREE Spring 2015 Conference. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED562106

article_title: Coaching Quality and Teachers' Implementation of the 4Rs Social-Emotional and Literacy Curriculum: Testing the Link between Two Levels of Intervention Fidelity
citation: Downer, J., Brown, J., Jimenez Herrera, M., Stuhlman, M., Bourassa, K., Gologor, B., & Wong, P. (2013). Coaching Quality and Teachers' Implementation of the 4Rs Social-Emotional and Literacy Curriculum: Testing the Link between Two Levels of Intervention Fidelity. SREE Spring 2013 Conference. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED563035
title: 4Rs (Reading, Writing, Respect, and Resolution) social-emotional and literacy curriculum
description: The 4Rs program is an integrated SEL and literacy curriculum for grades 3-5 with two primary components: a comprehensive 7-unit, 21 lesson, literacy-based curriculum in conflict resolution and social-emotional learning, and 25 hours of teacher training plus ongoing coaching. Each unit begins with a read-aloud of a children's book, followed by "Book Talk" discussion, writing, and role-playing, then "Applied Learning" lessons taught weekly for 30-45 minutes throughout the academic year.
requirements: 25 hours of teacher training plus ongoing coaching
target_learners: Students in grades 3-5, including regular education, special education, inclusion, and dual language classrooms
target_learning_goals: Skills in handling anger, listening, assertiveness, cooperation, negotiation, mediation, and building community
examples: Units open with a carefully chosen children's book read aloud to introduce the unit's main theme
key_sources: Downer, J., Brown, J., Jimenez Herrera, M., Stuhlman, M., Bourassa, K., Gologor, B., & Wong, P. (2013). Coaching Quality and Teachers' Implementation of the 4Rs Social-Emotional and Literacy Curriculum: Testing the Link between Two Levels of Intervention Fidelity. SREE Spring 2013 Conference. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED563032
